issues.where: d6 (Referral Note from Primary Care, released at start)
issues.problem: The referral note explicitly states 'Patient has expressed hesitation about anticoagulation due to a family history of intracranial hemorrhage on warfarin' — this discloses the reluctant/hidden fact f12 (brother's ICH on warfarin) and the critical psychosocial concern f24 before the learner ever asks. This should be removed from the artifact or replaced with a generic 'anticoagulation discussion requested' without revealing the family history reason.

issues.where: a12 result (STOP-BANG) and a13 result (home oximetry)
issues.problem: STOP-BANG is a self-report questionnaire that must be administered by asking the patient the component questions (snoring, witnessed apneas, etc.); handing back a finished score of 5/8 as an 'exam/test' result without the learner eliciting components (which match reluctant fact f15/f16) bypasses interview-based elicitation of hidden facts. Likewise a13 hands over overnight oximetry desaturation to 88% as if objectively measured/reviewed, but this is 'patient-reported' per the result text, meaning it is being disclosed as a record review though it is actually self-report that should normally emerge only through conversation. Both actions in effect hand over reluctant information (snoring/apnea awareness, nocturnal hypoxia) that otherwise requires rapport-building questions; fix by either making these true instrument reviews with a scored outcome sheet artifact or removing them as actions and leaving disclosure to the interview tier facts (f15, f16).

revised: d6: Removed the sentence explicitly disclosing the patient's family history of intracranial hemorrhage on warfarin (f12) and his specific hesitation reason; replaced with a generic 'anticoagulation discussion requested' phrase so f12/f24 remain learner-elicited via interview, not pre-disclosed in the referral note.

a12: Converted from a pre-scored STOP-BANG result (5/8) handed over as a completed test to an action describing that the component questions (snoring, witnessed apnea, daytime sleepiness, etc.) must be asked directly of the patient; removed the finished score and abnormal flag so disclosure of f15/f16 only happens through interview.

a13: Converted from a 'reviewed' overnight oximetry result (reporting desaturation to 88%) to an action prompting the learner to ask the patient about home oximetry/nocturnal symptoms, since this was self-report masquerading as a chart/device review; removed the abnormal flag and the specific desaturation figure from the action result so it surfaces only via the interview-tier facts.

a11: Recomputed CHA2DS2-VASc explicitly: hypertension (1) + diabetes (1) + age 61 (0, since 65-74 required for a point) + no CHF/stroke/vascular disease/female sex = total 2, consistent with the rest of the case (previous result text was muddled/self-contradictory); clarified wording while keeping the correct total of 2 and ~2.2%/year stroke risk, matching answerKey and plan.

chartAtStart: Added 'CHA2DS2-VASc 2' to the Problem list entry for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation for consistency with a11/answerKey, since the reviewer flagged the problem list as not reflecting the computed risk score used throughout the rest of the case.

o3: Reworded to make explicit that OSA screening (STOP-BANG) and nocturnal symptom history must be obtained via direct patient interview rather than chart review, consistent with the fixes to a12/a13.

Confirmed mismatches m1 and m2 remain valid and unaffected: their evidence derives from d7 (home BP/pulse log) and d1 (patch monitor), not from the removed/changed STOP-BANG, oximetry, or referral-note content, so no further edits were needed there.
